relevant_findings.topic: Caulking is a standalone LF-based line item, not embedded in painting specs
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior caulking is scoped as a separate line item from painting labor. Caulking applies across multiple surfaces (trim-to-siding, window perimeters, corner boards, penetrations, expansion joints) and is not attributable to a single painting spec. Measuring in LF (linear feet of joint) allows accurate estimation independent of the painting surface it borders. This matches the Doctrine integration note: 'Any exterior caulk scope auto-add as line item (separate from painting labor).'

relevant_findings.topic: Sealant type is the primary material and scheduling driver
relevant_findings.finding: Four paintable sealant types are in scope: acrylic_latex (paint immediately after skinning, 5-10 yr lifespan, low movement), siliconized_acrylic (paint immediately, 10-15 yr, improved water resistance), polyurethane (paint after 3-7 day cure, 15-25 yr, Class 25/50 movement), and hybrid_ms (paint after skin forms, 20-30 yr, Class 25 movement). Silicone is EXCLUDED — it is never paintable. Sealant type drives material cost, cure time scheduling impact, and movement capacity suitability.

relevant_findings.topic: Joint complexity drives production rate bifurcation
relevant_findings.finding: Two joint complexity tiers: simple_bead (gun-and-tool, no backer rod) at 100-150 LF/hr, and backer_rod (backer rod installation + sealant + tooling) at 75-100 LF/hr. Backer rod is required when joint width exceeds 3/8 inch to prevent three-sided adhesion and maintain proper width:depth ratio (2:1). Backer rod must be 25% larger than joint width for compression fit. Closed-cell foam is standard.

Sealant must bond only to two opposing sidewalls of the joint. Three-sided adhesion (sealant bonded to both sidewalls AND the joint bottom) causes premature cohesive failure because the sealant cannot stretch freely when the joint moves. Backer rod serves as a bond-breaker on the joint bottom. For joints too shallow for backer rod, bond-breaker tape on the joint bottom is the alternative. This is a non-negotiable quality standard — no exceptions.

relevant_findings.topic: Sequencing dependency: caulk after substrate primer, before finish coats
relevant_findings.finding: Correct sequence is: clean substrate, apply substrate primer if needed for sealant adhesion, apply caulk, allow full cure, then apply paint primer/finish coats over cured caulk. Painting over uncured caulk causes paint film cracking because caulk beads (~40 mils thick) shrink as they cure, while paint films (1-3 mils) cannot flex enough to accommodate the shrinkage. This sequencing rule creates a scheduling dependency — polyurethane sealant adds 3-7 days between caulk and finish coat.

relevant_findings.topic: Joint location categories for scope breakdown
relevant_findings.finding: Five exterior joint location categories: (1) trim_to_siding — where trim boards meet siding field, the most common joint type. (2) window_perimeter — casing-to-wall joints around window openings. (3) corner_board — vertical corner board joints at building corners. (4) penetration — joints around utility penetrations, pipes, vents, electrical boxes. (5) expansion — designed movement joints at material transitions or long runs. Each location may have different sealant type requirements based on expected movement.

relevant_findings.topic: Failure modes inform quality control requirements
relevant_findings.finding: Two primary failure modes: (1) Adhesive failure — sealant pulls away from substrate cleanly. Root causes: poor surface prep (dirt, oil, moisture), missing substrate primer, incompatible sealant-to-substrate pairing. (2) Cohesive failure — sealant tears internally while remaining bonded to both sides. Root causes: joint movement exceeded sealant rating (wrong movement class), joint too narrow for movement, UV aging causing embrittlement. Both modes inform mandatory inspection tasks.

relevant_findings.topic: No quality tier dimension for caulking
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike painting specs, caulking does not have a quality tier dimension (QT2-QT5). Caulking quality is driven by sealant_type selection (which determines durability, movement capacity, and lifespan) and joint_complexity (which determines whether backer rod and proper joint design are applied). There is no 'economy caulk' vs 'premium caulk' progression like paint quality tiers — every caulk joint either meets the standard or fails. The sealant_type dimension effectively replaces quality tier as the cost/quality driver.

relevant_findings.topic: Silicone is explicitly excluded from paintable scope
relevant_findings.finding: Silicone sealant (Class 50 movement, 20-50+ year lifespan) is the highest-performing sealant but repels all paint. It cannot be painted and paint will not adhere to silicone residue. If a joint requires painting, silicone must not be used. Silicone is applied AFTER painting is complete, only on non-paintable joints. If silicone was previously applied to a joint that now needs painting, the silicone must be completely removed — no solvent or primer can create adhesion over silicone.

relevant_findings.topic: Width:depth ratio 2:1 drives joint design tasks
relevant_findings.finding: Optimal sealant joint design is width twice the depth (2:1 ratio), with 1:1 as the minimum acceptable. Example: 1/2 inch wide joint requires 1/4 inch sealant depth. Joints deeper than ideal require backer rod to control depth. Joints wider than 3/8 inch are auto-flagged for backer rod. This geometry rule drives the joint_complexity dimension — simple_bead applies when natural joint geometry meets the 2:1 ratio without intervention.

research_corrections.original_prompt_value: Config dimensions list 3 sealant types: acrylic_latex, polyurethane, hybrid
research_corrections.corrected_value: 4 paintable sealant types: acrylic_latex, siliconized_acrylic, polyurethane, hybrid_ms
research_corrections.reason: Doctrine defines siliconized acrylic as a distinct paintable sealant type with improved water resistance and 10-15 year lifespan — it sits between acrylic_latex and polyurethane in performance. Omitting it would create a gap in the sealant selection spectrum.

research_corrections.corrected_value: No separate height/access modifier for caulking — shared cost assumption with painting spec
research_corrections.reason: Caulking at height does require ladder/scaffold access, but caulking is performed during the same access setup as painting. The painting spec (siding, trim) already carries the access modifier for that elevation. Adding a separate access modifier to caulking would double-count the access cost. Document as a shared cost assumption — caulking production rates assume access is already in place.

key_decisions.topic: Standalone spec — caulking as separate line item
key_decisions.decision: Exterior caulking is a standalone spec family (SF_CAULK_EXT), not embedded within trim, siding, or window painting specs. Caulking crosses all exterior surface boundaries and is a distinct trade operation with its own materials, production rates, and sequencing rules.
key_decisions.rationale: Caulking applies to joints between trim and siding, around windows, at corner boards, and at penetrations. Embedding it in any single surface spec would miss joints at other surfaces. A standalone line item ensures all joints are captured, priced, and sequenced correctly.
alternatives_considered: Embed caulking tasks within each adjacent surface spec (trim, siding, window)
Include caulking as a modifier on trim spec only

key_decisions.decision: All caulking is measured in linear feet (LF) of joint. This is the primary UOM for both scope takeoff and production rate calculation.
key_decisions.rationale: Caulking is inherently a linear operation — guns dispense sealant along a joint line. Production rates are published in LF/hr by industry sources. LF allows precise joint-by-joint takeoff and matches the PaintScope key format for edge measurements.

key_decisions.decision: This spec does NOT use a quality_tier (QT2-QT5) configuration dimension. Caulking quality is driven entirely by sealant_type and joint_complexity.
key_decisions.rationale: There is no meaningful 'economy caulk' vs 'premium caulk' progression. A caulk joint either has proper adhesion, correct width:depth ratio, and appropriate movement class — or it fails. The sealant_type dimension (acrylic_latex through hybrid_ms) provides the cost/durability spectrum. joint_complexity provides the labor intensity spectrum. Together they replace QT.
alternatives_considered: Map sealant types to QT3/QT4/QT5 equivalents

key_decisions.decision: sealant_type is the primary configuration dimension with 4 values: acrylic_latex, siliconized_acrylic, polyurethane, hybrid_ms. Silicone is excluded.
key_decisions.rationale: Sealant type drives material cost, cure time (scheduling impact), movement capacity (which joints it can serve), and lifespan. It is the single most impactful decision in the caulking scope. Silicone is excluded because it is never paintable — it belongs in a separate non-paint scope if needed.
alternatives_considered: Include silicone as a gated option with warnings

key_decisions.decision: joint_complexity has 2 values: simple_bead and backer_rod. This drives the production rate split and controls whether backer rod material and installation tasks are activated.
key_decisions.rationale: The 25-50% production rate difference between simple bead (100-150 LF/hr) and backer rod joints (75-100 LF/hr) is significant enough to warrant a configuration dimension rather than a modifier. Backer rod also adds material cost and a distinct installation task.
alternatives_considered: Single complexity with backer rod as a modifier

key_decisions.decision: Silicone sealant is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. This spec covers only paintable sealant joints. Silicone is never paintable and must be applied after all painting is complete.
key_decisions.rationale: Per doctrine, silicone repels paint and cannot be painted over. Including it in a spec that feeds into a painting workflow would create a scheduling and quality conflict. If a project needs silicone joints (e.g., non-painted metal flashing), that is a separate scope item outside this spec family.
alternatives_considered: Include silicone with a hard gate blocking paint-over

key_decisions.decision: When sealant_type = polyurethane, a mandatory 3-7 day cure gate is enforced before any paint/primer can be applied over the caulked joints. This is a scheduling constraint, not a production rate modifier.
key_decisions.rationale: Painting over uncured polyurethane causes 'flash cure' and surface bubbling from moisture in the paint. The cure gate is absolute — no exceptions regardless of weather, urgency, or tier. This impacts project scheduling and must be surfaced to the estimator as a scheduling dependency.
alternatives_considered: Treat as a warning rather than a hard gate

key_decisions.topic: Backer rod auto-add when joint > 3/8 inch wide
key_decisions.decision: When joint width exceeds 3/8 inch, joint_complexity automatically escalates to backer_rod. Backer rod diameter = joint width x 1.25. Closed-cell foam is the default type.
key_decisions.rationale: Joints wider than 3/8 inch without backer rod will have improper width:depth ratio and risk three-sided adhesion — both of which cause premature failure. The auto-add rule prevents estimators from accidentally scoping wide joints as simple_bead.
alternatives_considered: Let estimator override to simple_bead for wide joints

key_decisions.decision: All joints must be designed for two-sided adhesion only. Backer rod (or bond-breaker tape for shallow joints) is mandatory whenever the joint bottom would otherwise bond to the sealant. This is a non-negotiable quality standard.
key_decisions.rationale: Three-sided adhesion restricts sealant movement and causes premature cohesive failure. This is the most common cause of sealant failure in residential construction. The cost of backer rod is trivial compared to the cost of joint failure and re-caulk.
alternatives_considered: None — this is a universal industry standard

key_decisions.topic: Sequencing rule — after substrate primer, before finish coats
key_decisions.decision: Caulking must occur AFTER substrate primer (if applicable) and BEFORE finish coats. This sequencing rule is a hard constraint that must be surfaced in SOP modules and scheduling logic.
key_decisions.rationale: Sealant adhesion is improved on primed surfaces (primer provides a uniform bonding surface). Finish coats must cover the cured sealant to create a continuous weatherproof envelope. Violating this sequence causes either poor sealant adhesion (caulk before primer) or cracked paint film (paint before cure).
alternatives_considered: Caulk before any primer (rejected — adhesion risk)

key_decisions.topic: Joint locations categorized for scope breakdown
key_decisions.decision: Five joint location categories: trim_to_siding, window_perimeter, corner_board, penetration, expansion. Each location may have different sealant type requirements based on expected joint movement.
key_decisions.rationale: Different joint locations have different movement characteristics. Trim-to-siding joints are low movement (acrylic sufficient). Expansion joints require high movement capacity (polyurethane or hybrid). Categorizing locations allows the estimator to assign appropriate sealant types per location.

key_decisions.decision: Caulking does NOT carry its own height or access modifier. Access costs are shared with the painting spec that covers the same elevation.
key_decisions.rationale: Caulking is performed during the same access setup as painting — the scaffold, ladder, or lift is already in place for the painting spec. Adding a separate access modifier to caulking would double-count the access cost. Production rates assume access is already established.
alternatives_considered: Add a reduced access modifier (0.5x the painting access factor)

condition_drivers.name: Sealant Type
condition_drivers.impact: Primary driver — determines material cost, cure time before painting, movement capacity, and lifespan. Acrylic_latex is lowest cost/shortest life. Hybrid_ms is highest cost/longest life among paintable options. Polyurethane introduces 3-7 day cure gate.
condition_drivers.notes: Silicone excluded (never paintable). Per project, multiple sealant types may be used — e.g., acrylic for low-movement trim joints, polyurethane for expansion joints.

condition_drivers.name: Joint Complexity
condition_drivers.impact: Drives production rate split: simple_bead = 100-150 LF/hr, backer_rod = 75-100 LF/hr. Also drives material activation (backer rod material) and task activation (backer rod installation task). Auto-escalates to backer_rod when joint width > 3/8 inch.
condition_drivers.notes: Per project, both complexity tiers may coexist — some joints are simple bead, others require backer rod.

paintable_items.name: Exterior Caulk Joint
paintable_items.description: A linear joint between exterior building components requiring sealant. Measured in linear feet. Not a painted surface — the sealant bead IS the deliverable. Downstream painting specs apply finish coats over the cured sealant.
paintable_items.ps_key_source: Derived from scope — sum of joint LF across all joint locations. No single PS_EXT key exists for caulk LF; the estimator captures joint quantities during takeoff or derives from trim/opening LF keys.
paintable_items.notes: This is a non-coating item. The 'paintable' designation is nominal — the item represents the caulked joint, which is subsequently painted by adjacent surface specs.

paintscope_key_mapping.description: Caulk joint LF does not have a dedicated PS_EXT key. Joint quantities are derived from takeoff of adjacent surfaces or captured directly during scope. The following PS_EXT keys provide the geometry from which caulk LF can be estimated.

derived_from_keys.derivation: Window perimeter joints are approximately equal to window casing LF (caulk runs along the casing-to-wall joint)
Door perimeter joints are approximately equal to door casing LF
Corner board joints — caulk runs both edges of the corner board (2x corner LF)
Band board top and bottom joints (2x band LF)
Fascia-to-soffit joint — approximately equal to fascia LF

direct_capture_keys.description: Total linear feet of caulk joints in scope — entered directly by estimator when derived calculation is not appropriate
Subset of total joint LF requiring backer rod installation (joints > 3/8 inch wide)
direct_capture_keys.default_derivation: If not provided, defaults to 0 (all joints treated as simple_bead)

spec_inputs.name: Total Caulk Joint Linear Feet
spec_inputs.description: Total linear feet of all caulk joints in exterior scope

spec_inputs.name: Backer Rod Joint Linear Feet
spec_inputs.description: Subset of total joint LF requiring backer rod (joints > 3/8 inch wide)

spec_inputs.name: Sealant Type
spec_inputs.description: Primary sealant type for paintable joints

production_rates.description: Production rates for exterior caulking tasks. All rates in LF per man-hour at ground level with access in place.

rate_tables.description: Simple bead caulking — gun and tool, no backer rod
rate_tables.notes: Midpoint 125 LF/hr used as QT3-equivalent baseline. Range varies by joint access and tooling difficulty.

rate_tables.description: Backer rod installation + caulking — insert rod, gun sealant, tool
rate_tables.notes: Midpoint ~87 LF/hr. Includes backer rod insertion (rod sizing, compression fit) plus sealant application and tooling.

rate_tables.description: Joint preparation — cleaning, scraping old caulk residue, drying
rate_tables.notes: For NC joints, prep is minimal (dust/debris removal). Rate is for clean new joints. Repaint caulk removal would be significantly slower but is outside NC scope.

material_systems.description: Material systems for exterior caulking. Each sealant type is a distinct material selection. No primer/finish pairing — caulk IS the product.

systems.name: Acrylic Latex Sealant
systems.notes: Lowest cost option. Adequate for standard trim-to-siding joints on wood-frame construction.

systems.name: Siliconized Acrylic Sealant
systems.best_for: Improved water resistance over acrylic, standard joints
systems.notes: Mid-range option. Better water resistance and flexibility than straight acrylic.

systems.name: Polyurethane Sealant
systems.notes: High performance but scheduling impact. 3-7 day cure gate before painting. Lower yield per tube due to larger joint widths typically served.

systems.name: Hybrid MS Polymer Sealant
systems.best_for: Premium: combines silicone durability with paintability
systems.notes: Highest cost paintable option. Best long-term performance. Shorter paint wait than polyurethane.

consumables.name: Sealant Tube (10.1 oz)
consumables.notes: Standard 10.1 oz cartridge. Yield assumes 1/4 inch bead on standard joint. Wider joints reduce yield to ~25 LF/tube.

consumables.name: Closed-Cell Backer Rod
consumables.notes: Sold in rolls (20-100 ft). Multiple diameters: 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 3/4, 1 inch. Size = joint width x 1.25.

consumables.name: Caulk Gun (ratchet or smooth-rod)
consumables.notes: Reusable tool. Smooth-rod preferred for professional use — better bead control. One per crew member.

consumables.name: Masking Tape for Clean Lines
consumables.notes: Optional — used for clean-line caulk joints on visible surfaces. Not all joints require tape masking.

protection_zones.name: Ground Surface Below Work Area
protection_zones.description: Drop cloth directly below caulking work to catch sealant drips and cut-off bead waste. Minimal coverage — caulking produces very little overspray. Small drops only.
protection_zones.activation: Always active when caulking is in scope

protection_zones.name: Adjacent Finished Surfaces
protection_zones.description: Tape along joint edges on finished surfaces to create a clean sealant line. Applies when caulking against already-painted or factory-finished surfaces where sealant smear would be visible.
protection_zones.activation: Conditional — active when caulking against finished surfaces

exclusions.description: Silicone sealant is excluded from this spec. Silicone is never paintable. Non-paintable joint sealing (e.g., metal flashing, glass-to-frame, post-paint joints) is outside scope.
exclusions.reason: Silicone repels paint — incompatible with painting workflow

exclusions.description: Structural adhesive joints, fire-stop sealants, and below-grade waterproofing sealants are excluded. These are specialty applications outside the painting trade.
exclusions.reason: Different trade, different materials, different standards

exclusions.description: Access/staging costs (ladder, scaffold, lift) are excluded from this spec. Access is shared with the painting spec covering the same elevation.
exclusions.reason: Per KD-012 — caulking is performed during painting access setup. Double-counting access would inflate estimates.

exclusions.description: Old caulk removal for repaint scope is excluded from this NC spec. This spec covers new construction caulking only — joints are open and clean.
exclusions.reason: NC joints have no existing sealant to remove. Repaint caulk removal would be a separate SF_CAULK_EXT_RP spec.

cross_spec_dependencies.description: Caulking must occur AFTER substrate primer (from painting spec) and BEFORE finish coats (from painting spec). This creates an inter-spec sequencing dependency. The painting spec's SOP must include a 'caulk complete' gate check before proceeding to finish coats.
When sealant_type = polyurethane, a 3-7 day cure gate delays finish coat application on ALL adjacent painting specs. This impacts project scheduling and must be visible in the estimate timeline.

sop_module_sketch.description: Preliminary module structure for SOP. Caulking is a simple, focused workflow with fewer modules than painting specs.

modules.name: Protection Setup
tasks_sketch: TSK_CAULK_PROTECT_GROUND — Lay drop cloth below work area
TSK_CAULK_MASK_ADJACENT — Tape adjacent finished surfaces for clean lines (conditional)

modules.name: Joint Preparation
tasks_sketch: TSK_CAULK_JOINT_CLEAN — Clean joint of dust, debris, loose material
TSK_CAULK_BACKER_ROD_INSTALL — Install backer rod in joints > 3/8 inch (conditional on joint_complexity = backer_rod)

modules.name: Sealant Application
tasks_sketch: TSK_CAULK_APPLY_BEAD — Apply sealant bead using caulk gun
TSK_CAULK_TOOL_JOINT — Tool (smooth) sealant bead for proper profile and adhesion

modules.name: Joint Inspection
tasks_sketch: TSK_CAULK_INSPECT — Inspect all joints for continuity, adhesion, proper tooling, no voids

modules.name: Cleanup and Protection Teardown
tasks_sketch: TSK_CAULK_CLEANUP — Remove drop cloths, dispose of waste caulk, clean tools

task_sketch.description: Preliminary task list. Intentionally lean — caulking is a simple operation. Task count target: 8-12 tasks.

tasks.description: Lay drop cloth below caulking work area
Tape adjacent finished surfaces for clean sealant lines
tasks.conditional: Active when caulking against finished surfaces

tasks.description: Clean joint of dust, debris, loose material
Install closed-cell backer rod in joints > 3/8 inch wide. Size rod = joint width x 1.25.
Apply sealant bead to simple joints (no backer rod) using caulk gun
Apply sealant bead to backer rod joints using caulk gun
Tool (smooth) sealant bead for proper concave profile and substrate contact. Bundled into apply rate — not a separate time adder.
tasks.notes: Tooling is integral to the apply task. Rate includes tooling time.

tasks.description: Inspect all joints for continuity, proper adhesion, no voids, correct profile
Remove masking tape from adjacent surfaces
Remove drop cloths, dispose of waste caulk tubes, clean caulk gun

scheduling_gates.blocks: All finish coat tasks in adjacent painting specs
scheduling_gates.description: Polyurethane sealant requires 3-7 day full cure before any paint or primer can be applied over it. Water from paint causes flash cure and surface bubbling. This is an absolute scheduling gate — no exceptions.
scheduling_gates.resolution: Schedule caulking early in the project. Use acrylic or hybrid if polyurethane cure time is unacceptable for the schedule.

scheduling_gates.prerequisite: Substrate primer on adjacent surfaces must be applied before caulking
scheduling_gates.description: Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces than bare substrates. Priming first also allows the primer to seal the substrate, preventing sealant adhesion failure from substrate outgassing.

movement_class_routing.description: Sealant type selection based on expected joint movement. This is a decision support table for estimators.

open_questions.question: Should a dedicated PS_EXT key be created for caulk joint LF (e.g., PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.CAULK_TOTAL), or is derivation from trim/opening LF keys sufficient?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether PaintScope needs a new key type or whether the estimator manually captures caulk LF
open_questions.recommendation: Create IN_LF_CAULK_JOINT_TOTAL as a direct capture input for now. Evaluate a PS_EXT key if caulk estimation is frequently derived from geometry.

open_questions.question: Should this spec support per-location sealant type assignment (e.g., acrylic for trim joints, polyurethane for expansion joints on the same project)?
open_questions.impact: If yes, the spec needs a location-by-sealant-type matrix rather than a single sealant_type dimension
open_questions.recommendation: Defer to v2. For v1, use a single dominant sealant_type per project. Note that expansion joints requiring polyurethane can be flagged as a separate line if needed.
